cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Bring Back Everything
cards.instruction: Return early details in altered forms until the scene feels like it has been building toward one unavoidable consequence.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You called the spare chair unnecessary, then put the birthday cake on it. Our guest has the piano stool, and the pianist needs it back.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The cake needs a flat place. I can't put it on someone's lap.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then serve the cake and free the chair. Move the guest back before asking the pianist to play, please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We can't cut it until he's played Happy Birthday.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then ask the guest to stand for one verse. Pianist on the stool, song, cake, chair. Please give the guest the first slice; that spare chair has kept them standing for their own birthday.

reason: Use explicit ceremony order to make the earlier furniture decisions converge on a brief standing guest, with no impossible piano/window geography.
